group.title: Professional verbs
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: To give something officially for a particular purpose.
examples: The city will {allocate} funds for new schools.
wrong: To allocate money is to keep it all and give none to any purpose.

words.meaning: To publicly support an idea or a plan.
examples: She will {advocate} for better public transport.
wrong: To advocate an idea is to argue strongly against it.

words.meaning: To express ideas clearly in words.
wrong: To articulate an idea is to hide it and say nothing.

words.meaning: To collect information from different places and put it together.
examples: I will {compile} the data into one report.
wrong: To compile a report is to delete all the information from it.

words.meaning: To be or form something.
wrong: Ten percent constitutes the whole of the workforce.

words.meaning: To make something shorter or less.
examples: The company had to {curtail} its travel budget.
wrong: To curtail a budget is to make it much larger.

words.meaning: To get something from a source.
wrong: To derive a word is to invent it from nothing, with no source.

words.meaning: To make secret information known.
wrong: To disclose a secret is to keep it hidden forever.

words.meaning: To make people obey a rule or a law.
wrong: To enforce a law is to ignore it and let people break it.

words.meaning: To make a process easier.
wrong: To facilitate a process is to make it harder and slower.

words.meaning: To encourage something to grow or develop.
examples: Good teachers {foster} a love of reading.
wrong: To foster a skill is to stop it from developing.

words.meaning: To make it difficult for something to happen.
wrong: To hinder a task is to help it finish more quickly.

words.meaning: To include something as part of a whole.
examples: We will {incorporate} your ideas into the plan.
wrong: To incorporate an idea is to leave it out of the plan completely.

words.meaning: To make something less harmful or severe.
examples: Trees help to {mitigate} the effects of heat.
wrong: To mitigate a problem is to make it worse.

words.meaning: To watch over a task or people to be sure all is done properly.
wrong: To oversee a project is to ignore it completely.

words.meaning: To put right something that is wrong.
examples: We will {rectify} the mistake at once.
wrong: To rectify an error is to repeat it again and again.

words.meaning: To make something stronger.
wrong: To reinforce a wall is to make it weaker.

words.meaning: To examine something very carefully.
wrong: To scrutinize a paper is to glance at it for a second and ignore the details.

words.meaning: To make a process simpler and more efficient.
examples: We want to {streamline} the application process.
wrong: To streamline a process is to make it longer and more complicated.

words.meaning: To make something weaker or less effective.
wrong: To undermine confidence is to build it up.

words.meaning: To provide enough space or what is needed for someone.
examples: The hotel can {accommodate} three hundred guests.
wrong: A room that accommodates fifty people holds only two.

words.meaning: To accept that something is true or exists.
wrong: To acknowledge a mistake is to deny that it happened.

words.meaning: To follow a rule or a plan exactly.
examples: All staff must {adhere} to the safety rules.
wrong: To adhere to a rule is to break it on purpose.

words.meaning: To make pain or a problem less severe.
wrong: To alleviate pain is to make it much stronger.

words.meaning: To find out something for certain.
examples: The police tried to {ascertain} the facts.
wrong: To ascertain a fact is to guess it without checking.

words.meaning: To pass from person to person or place to place.
examples: Please {circulate} the report to the whole team.
wrong: To circulate a report is to keep it locked in a drawer.

words.meaning: To obey a rule or request.
wrong: To comply with a rule is to refuse to follow it.

words.meaning: To organize and carry out an activity.
wrong: To conduct a survey is to cancel it before it starts.

words.meaning: To combine things into one stronger whole.
examples: The bank plans to {consolidate} its branches.
wrong: To consolidate offices is to split them into many tiny ones.

words.meaning: To claim that something is true.
examples: She {contends} that the law is unfair.
wrong: To contend a point is to agree with every other person.

words.meaning: To bring people together for a meeting.
wrong: To convene a meeting is to send everyone away.

words.meaning: To make someone decide not to do something.
wrong: To deter people is to invite them and encourage them to come.

words.meaning: To publicly support a person or a plan.
wrong: To endorse a product is to warn people against it.

words.meaning: Not required to follow a rule or to pay.
wrong: People who are exempt from a fee must pay a higher fee.

words.meaning: To complete the last details of something.
wrong: To finalize a plan is to start it from the beginning.

words.meaning: To describe the main points of something.
examples: I will {outline} the plan in a few words.
wrong: To outline a plan is to explain every small detail at great length.

words.meaning: To follow or try to achieve something.
examples: She decided to {pursue} a career in law.
wrong: To pursue a goal is to run away from it.

words.meaning: To make an agreement official by signing or voting.
examples: The parliament voted to {ratify} the treaty.
wrong: To ratify a treaty is to tear it up and cancel it.

words.meaning: To officially cancel something.
wrong: To revoke a license is to give a new one.

words.meaning: To keep something going over time.
examples: It is hard to {sustain} growth for ten years.
wrong: To sustain growth is to stop it at once.
